title: The Fragmented Narrative
text:
Postmodern fiction often rejects the notion of a single, coherent narrative voice. Writers such as Italo Calvino and Jorge Luis Borges constructed texts that fold back upon themselves, inviting readers to question the very act of reading. In such works, the author's authority is deliberately undermined, and the reader becomes a co-creator of meaning. The result is an ambiguity that many critics regard as the defining feature of the movement.

Experimental literature extends this skepticism into the physical form of the book. Some texts include blank pages, typographical irregularities, or footnotes that outnumber the main body. Such devices compel the reader to navigate the work nonlinearly, reassembling fragments into a provisional whole. Consequently, the reading experience becomes less a matter of arriving at conclusions than of tolerating uncertainty.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do many critics consider the defining feature of postmodern fiction?
According to paragraph two, which devices can experimental texts include?
What can be inferred about the reader's role in experimental texts?
options: The reader must passively accept the author's conclusions
The reader actively constructs meaning from fragments
The reader is excluded from interpreting the work
The reader's role is limited to identifying the author

questions.text: What is the author's likely attitude toward the uncertainty of postmodern literature?
options: Strongly hostile to it, seeing it as a failure of literature
Indifferent, since it has no real effect on reading
Accepting it as a central part of the reading experience
Concerned that it makes all books unreadable

vocabulary.definition: doubt about whether something is true or valuable
the quality of having more than one possible meaning
small parts broken off from a whole
not in a straight sequence from beginning to end

paragraph_translations: La ficción posmoderna a menudo rechaza la noción de una única voz narrativa coherente. Escritores como Italo Calvino y Jorge Luis Borges construyeron textos que se pliegan sobre sí mismos, invitando al lector a cuestionar el propio acto de leer. En estas obras, la autoridad del autor se socava deliberadamente y el lector se convierte en co-creador del significado. El resultado es una ambigüedad que muchos críticos consideran el rasgo definitorio del movimiento.

La literatura experimental extiende este escepticismo a la forma física del libro. Algunos textos incluyen páginas en blanco, irregularidades tipográficas o notas al pie que superan en número al cuerpo principal. Tales recursos obligan al lector a recorrer la obra de forma no lineal, reensamblando fragmentos en un todo provisional. En consecuencia, la experiencia de lectura consiste menos en llegar a conclusiones que en tolerar la incertidumbre.
